learn.hook: Halls, trains, candles and consecutive numbers — so many everyday puzzles secretly hide an x²!
points: Many situations give an equation with x²: areas of rectangles (length × breadth), products of two numbers, speed–time problems and cost problems.
Steps: call the unknown x, write the other quantities using x, form the equation from the given fact, and bring it to the form ax² + bx + c = 0.
History: Babylonians could find two positive numbers with a given sum and product. Brahmagupta (598–665 CE) gave an explicit formula for ax² + bx = c.
Later Sridharacharya (about 1025 CE) derived the quadratic formula by completing the square (as quoted by Bhaskara II).

example.q: A rectangular hall's length is 3 m more than its breadth, and its area is 180 m². Write a quadratic equation for the breadth.
steps: Let the breadth be x m, so the length is (x + 3) m

learn.reallife: Architects use quadratic equations to fit a room of a given area into a plot, and Indian mathematicians were solving them over a thousand years ago!

games.title: History and modelling
items: Brahmagupta gave an explicit formula to solve ax² + bx = c.
Brahmagupta (598–665 CE) gave such a formula.
Sridharacharya derived the quadratic formula by completing the square.
Around 1025 CE, as quoted by Bhaskara II.
The area of a rectangle with sides x and x + 5 gives a linear equation.
x(x + 5) = x² + 5x, which has an x² term.
Babylonians could find two positive numbers with a given sum and product.
This is the same as solving a quadratic equation.
Every word problem on speed gives a quadratic equation.
Only some do — for example when the time changes with the speed.

quiz.q: A rectangular hall's length is 3 m more than its breadth x, and its area is 180 m². Which equation fits?
quiz.explain: Area = x(x + 3) = 180, which gives x² + 3x − 180 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Adds the sides (perimeter idea) instead of multiplying for area

quiz.q: The product of two consecutive odd numbers is 143. If the smaller is x, which equation fits?
quiz.explain: Consecutive odd numbers differ by 2: x(x + 2) = 143, so x² + 2x − 143 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Uses x + 1 for the next odd number

quiz.q: A train covers 480 km at a steady speed of x km/h. If its speed were 8 km/h less, it would take 3 hours more. Which equation gives x?
quiz.mistake: Gets the sign wrong when subtracting the two times

quiz.q: Meena makes x candles in a day. Each candle costs ₹(40 − x) to make, and the day's total cost is ₹300. Which equation fits?
quiz.explain: Total cost = x(40 − x) = 300, so 40x − x² = 300, i.e. x² − 40x + 300 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply the cost per candle by the number of candles

quiz.q: Who derived the quadratic formula by completing the square, as quoted by Bhaskara II?
quiz.explain: Sridharacharya (about 1025 CE) derived the formula by completing the square; Bhaskara II quoted it.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Brahmagupta's earlier formula with Sridharacharya's method

quiz.q: Brahmagupta gave an explicit formula to solve equations of which form?
quiz.explain: Brahmagupta (598–665 CE) gave an explicit formula for quadratic equations of the form ax² + bx = c.
quiz.mistake: Thinks Brahmagupta worked only with linear equations

quiz.q: The squares of two consecutive positive integers add up to 61. If the smaller is x, which equation in standard form fits?
quiz.mistake: Writes (x + 1)² as x² + 1

quiz.q: A right triangle has hypotenuse 13 cm, and its height is 7 cm less than its base x. Which equation fits?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the middle term when squaring (x − 7)

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How does a story about a hall's area turn into a quadratic equation?' Explain to Gappu.
teach.praise: Chirp! Name the unknown x, use the fact to multiply things out, and get ax² + bx + c = 0!
teach.nudge: Which step makes the x² appear — and what form should I end with?

learn.hook: Split the middle term, pull out common factors, and a quadratic breaks neatly into two easy pieces!
points: A quadratic equation has the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.
A root is a value of x that makes the equation true. A quadratic equation has at most two roots.
To factorise ax² + bx + c, find two numbers whose product is ac and whose sum is b, and use them to split the middle term.
If (x − p)(x − q) = 0, then x = p or x = q, because a product is zero only when one factor is zero.
Never divide both sides by x — you may lose the root x = 0. Bring all terms to one side instead.

steps: ac = 2 × 3 = 6; two numbers with product 6 and sum −5 are −2 and −3

learn.reallife: Designers of a rectangular rangoli or garden with a fixed area often end up with a quadratic equation to find its sides.

games.title: Match the equation to its roots
Quadratic or not?
items: x(x + 1) = x² + 5 is a quadratic equation.
The x² terms cancel, leaving x = 5, which is linear.
x² = 0 has the root 0.
0² = 0, so x = 0 is a root (repeated).
In 3x² − 7 = 0, the value of b is 0.
There is no x term, so b = 0.
To factorise x² + 7x + 12, we need two numbers with product 12 and sum 7.
3 and 4 work: (x + 3)(x + 4).
If (x − 4)(x + 1) = 0, then x = −4 or x = 1.
Each factor is zero when x = 4 or x = −1.
A quadratic equation can have three different roots.
A quadratic equation has at most two roots.

quiz.q: Which of these is a quadratic equation?
quiz.explain: (x + 1)² = 2x + 5 becomes x² + 2x + 1 = 2x + 5, that is x² − 4 = 0, which has degree 2. In x² + 3x = x² − 1 the x² terms cancel, leaving a linear equation.
quiz.mistake: Judges by the look of the equation without simplifying it

quiz.q: What are the roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0?
quiz.explain: −3 and −4 have product 12 and sum −7, so x² − 7x + 12 = (x − 3)(x − 4). The roots are 3 and 4.
quiz.mistake: Picks a pair with product 12 but the wrong sum, or flips the signs

quiz.q: What are the roots of 6x² − x − 2 = 0?
quiz.explain: ac = −12; the numbers −4 and 3 have product −12 and sum −1. So 6x² − 4x + 3x − 2 = 2x(3x − 2) + 1(3x − 2) = (2x + 1)(3x − 2).
quiz.mistake: Gets the signs of the roots the wrong way round

quiz.q: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 132. What is the smaller integer?
quiz.explain: x(x + 1) = 132 gives x² + x − 132 = 0 = (x + 12)(x − 11). Since x is positive, x = 11 (and 11 × 12 = 132).
quiz.mistake: Gives the larger integer, or keeps the negative root

quiz.q: A rectangular mat is 4 m longer than it is wide, and its area is 60 m². What is its width?
quiz.explain: b(b + 4) = 60 gives b² + 4b − 60 = 0 = (b + 10)(b − 6). Width cannot be negative, so b = 6 m (length 10 m).
quiz.mistake: Gives the length (10 m) instead of the width

quiz.q: If x = 2 is a root of x² + kx + 6 = 0, what is k?
quiz.mistake: Loses the minus sign when moving 10 across

quiz.q: Kabir solves x² = 5x by dividing both sides by x and gets x = 5. Which root did he lose?
quiz.explain: x² − 5x = 0 gives x(x − 5) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 5. Dividing by x threw away x = 0.
quiz.mistake: Divides by a variable that could be zero

quiz.q: What are the roots of 4x² − 4x + 1 = 0?
quiz.explain: 4x² − 4x + 1 = (2x − 1)², so 2x − 1 = 0 twice. Both roots are 1/2.
quiz.mistake: Gets the sign of the root wrong

teach.ask: Gappu waves a quadratic equation: 'How do I break x² − 5x + 6 = 0 into pieces and find x?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Split the middle term using product and sum, then set each bracket to zero. Brilliant!
teach.nudge: Which two numbers do I look for, and what do I do with each bracket?

learn.hook: Surds and fractions in an equation look scary — but the same splitting trick still works!
points: A root α of ax² + bx + c = 0 is a number with aα² + bα + c = 0. The roots of the equation are exactly the zeros of the polynomial ax² + bx + c.
On a graph, the roots are the x-coordinates where y = ax² + bx + c meets the x-axis.
With fractions: multiply every term by the LCM of the denominators first, then factorise.
With surds like √2x² + 3x + √2: ac = √2 × √2 = 2, so look for two numbers with product 2 and sum 3 (2 and 1).
Equations like x − 1/x = 3/2 become quadratics after multiplying by x (with x ≠ 0).

steps: ac = √2 × √2 = 2; numbers with product 2 and sum 3: 2 and 1

learn.reallife: Engineers often get equations with √3 or fractions from triangle and circuit measurements — and must solve them exactly.

items.text: If p(4) = 0, then 4 is a ___ of p(x) = 0

games.title: Match the equation to its roots

quiz.q: Is x = 3 a root of x² − 5x + 6 = 0?
options: No, because 3 is not a factor of 6
quiz.explain: Put x = 3: 3² − 5(3) + 6 = 9 − 15 + 6 = 0. The equation is satisfied, so 3 is a root.
quiz.mistake: Does not substitute carefully, or uses factors of 6 as a shortcut

quiz.q: The zeros of p(x) = x² − 9x + 20 are 4 and 5. What are the roots of x² − 9x + 20 = 0?
quiz.explain: The roots of p(x) = 0 are the same as the zeros of p(x): 4 and 5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks roots and zeros are different numbers

quiz.q: Which value is a root of 2x² + x − 6 = 0?
quiz.mistake: Gets the sign of the root wrong

quiz.q: What are the roots of √2x² + 3x + √2 = 0?
quiz.mistake: Drops the minus signs when solving each bracket

quiz.q: Ria multiplies x² − (3/2)x + 1/2 = 0 by 2 and factorises. What roots does she get?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only some of the terms by 2

quiz.q: Solve x − 1/x = 3/2 (x ≠ 0). What are the roots?
quiz.explain: Multiply by 2x: 2x² − 2 = 3x → 2x² − 3x − 2 = 0 → (2x + 1)(x − 2) = 0, so x = 2 or x = −1/2.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply the 1/x term by 2x

quiz.q: The graph of y = x² − 4x − 5 cuts the x-axis at (−1, 0) and (5, 0). What are the roots of x² − 4x − 5 = 0?
quiz.explain: The roots are the x-coordinates of the points where the graph meets the x-axis: −1 and 5.
quiz.mistake: Reads off the wrong coordinates

quiz.q: Which is a root of √3x² − 2x − √3 = 0?
quiz.mistake: Picks the right size but the wrong sign

teach.ask: Gappu sees x² − (3/2)x + 1/2 = 0 and panics about the fractions. How would you solve it, and how are its roots linked to zeros?
teach.praise: Tweet! Clear the fractions, factorise, and the roots are the polynomial's zeros!
teach.nudge: What should I do first to get rid of the fractions?

learn.hook: Can't factorise? No problem! One formula cracks every quadratic equation that has real roots.
points: For ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0), the roots are x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)] / 2a.
The quantity D = b² − 4ac is called the discriminant.
The formula gives real roots only when D ≥ 0.
First write the equation in standard form, then read a, b and c with their signs.
In word problems, reject roots that make no sense, like a negative speed or length.

example.q: Solve 2x² + x − 6 = 0 using the quadratic formula.

learn.reallife: Rocket scientists and bridge engineers use the quadratic formula to find times and lengths that don't factorise nicely.

items.text: In the quadratic formula, the denominator is ___

quiz.q: Use the quadratic formula to solve x² − 2x − 15 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Uses +b instead of −b in the formula

quiz.q: What is the discriminant of 3x² − 4x − 4 = 0?
quiz.mistake: Treats −4ac as −48 instead of +48

quiz.q: What are the roots of x² + 4x + 1 = 0?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide every term by 2a, or drops the minus on b

quiz.q: What is the larger root of 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0?
quiz.explain: D = 9 + 40 = 49, so x = (3 ± 7)/4, giving 5/2 or −1. The larger is 5/2.
quiz.mistake: Divides by a instead of 2a

quiz.q: Before using the formula on x² = 3x + 10, what are a, b and c?
quiz.explain: Rewrite it as x² − 3x − 10 = 0. Then a = 1, b = −3 and c = −10.
quiz.mistake: Reads a, b, c before bringing everything to one side

quiz.q: A train covers 300 km at a steady speed. If it went 10 km/h faster, the trip would take 1 hour less. What is its speed in km/h?
quiz.mistake: Gives the faster speed 60 km/h instead of the actual speed

quiz.q: A number plus its reciprocal equals 10/3. What could the number be?
quiz.mistake: Makes a sign error with the reciprocal

quiz.q: What is the repeated root of 9x² − 6x + 1 = 0?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the minus in −b/2a, or divides by a only

teach.ask: Gappu can't factorise 2x² + x − 6 = 0: 'Is there a formula that always works?'
teach.praise: Chirp! −b plus or minus root of the discriminant, all over 2a. I'll never be stuck again!
teach.nudge: What goes under the square root, and what do I divide by?

learn.hook: Before solving, the discriminant whispers a secret: two roots, one root, or none at all!
points: D = b² − 4ac decides the nature of the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0.
D > 0: two distinct real roots.
D = 0: two equal real roots, each equal to −b/2a.
D < 0: no real roots.
On a graph, D > 0 means the parabola cuts the x-axis twice, D = 0 means it touches once, and D < 0 means it does not meet the x-axis.

example.q: Find k so that kx² − 6x + 1 = 0 has two equal roots.

learn.reallife: Before building, an architect can check with the discriminant whether a park with a given perimeter and area is even possible.

games.title: Discriminant true or false
items: If D < 0, the equation has no real roots.
The square root of a negative number is not real.
If D = 0, each root equals −b/2a.
With D = 0 the ± part disappears, leaving −b/2a.
x² + 4 = 0 has the real roots 2 and −2.
D = 0 − 16 < 0, so it has no real roots. 2² + 4 = 8, not 0.
Every quadratic equation has at least one real root.
x² + 1 = 0 has none, since D = −4.
If a and c have opposite signs, the equation has two distinct real roots.
Then −4ac is positive, so D = b² − 4ac > 0.
If D > 0, the parabola touches the x-axis at exactly one point.
D > 0 means it cuts the x-axis at two points.

quiz.q: What is the nature of the roots of 2x² − 4x + 3 = 0?
options: One positive and one negative root
quiz.explain: D = 16 − 24 = −8, which is negative, so there are no real roots.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply by 4 in 4ac

quiz.q: For what positive value of k does x² + kx + 16 = 0 have equal roots?
quiz.explain: Equal roots need D = 0: k² − 64 = 0, so k = 8 (taking the positive value).
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 4 in 4ac and gets k = 4

quiz.q: What is the discriminant of 5x² − 3x + 1 = 0?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4ac instead of subtracting it

quiz.q: For which values of k does 2x² + 3x + k = 0 have no real roots?
quiz.explain: No real roots need D < 0: 9 − 8k < 0, so k > 9/8.
quiz.mistake: Flips the inequality sign

quiz.q: kx² + 4x + 1 = 0 has equal roots. What is the repeated root?
quiz.explain: D = 16 − 4k = 0 gives k = 4. The root is −b/2a = −4/8 = −1/2.
quiz.mistake: Drops the minus sign in −b/2a

quiz.q: Can a rectangular park have perimeter 40 m and area 120 m²?
options: No, because the discriminant is negative
No, because the area is too small
quiz.explain: l + b = 20 and lb = 120 give l² − 20l + 120 = 0. D = 400 − 480 = −80 < 0, so no such park exists. (12 × 10 has perimeter 44, and 15 × 8 has perimeter 46.)
quiz.mistake: Checks only the area and forgets the perimeter

quiz.q: Which equation has two distinct real roots?
quiz.explain: For 2x² + 5x − 3 = 0, D = 25 + 24 = 49 > 0. x² + x + 1 has D = −3, x² − 4x + 4 has D = 0 and x² + 3 has D = −12.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a perfect square like x² − 4x + 4 gives two different roots

quiz.q: A quadratic equation has two equal real roots. What does the graph of y = ax² + bx + c do?
options: Cuts the x-axis at two points
Touches the x-axis at exactly one point
quiz.explain: Equal roots mean D = 0, so the parabola just touches the x-axis at x = −b/2a.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up equal roots with two distinct roots

teach.ask: Gappu wonders: 'How can I tell how many roots a quadratic has without solving it?'
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! Positive D gives two roots, zero gives equal roots, negative gives none. Super!
teach.nudge: What happens when the discriminant is zero, or negative?

topics.title: Check the nature first, then solve — chapter recap

learn.hook: Before you dive into the formula, a quick look at D tells you whether there's any real answer to find!
points: Step 1: write the equation in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0) and find D = b² − 4ac.
Step 2: D > 0 → two distinct real roots; D = 0 → two equal roots, each −b/2a; D < 0 → no real roots (stop here).
Step 3: if D ≥ 0, find the roots: x = (−b ± √D)/2a.
Recap of methods: factorisation when it splits nicely, the quadratic formula always (when D ≥ 0).

example.q: Find the nature of the roots of 2x² − 6x + 3 = 0 and, if real, find them.
steps: D = 36 − 24 = 12 > 0, so two distinct real roots

learn.reallife: Before building a ramp of a given area, an engineer checks D — if it is negative, the design is impossible, so no time is wasted!

games.title: Sort by the nature of the roots

quiz.q: What is the nature of the roots of 2x² − 6x + 3 = 0, and what are they?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide the whole top by 2a = 4

quiz.q: 2x² − 2√2x + 1 = 0 has D = 0. What is its repeated root?
quiz.mistake: Uses b/2a and gets the sign wrong

quiz.q: What can you say about the roots of x² + x + 2 = 0?
quiz.explain: D = 1² − 4(1)(2) = 1 − 8 = −7 < 0, so there are no real roots.
quiz.mistake: Calculates b² + 4ac instead of b² − 4ac

quiz.q: x² − 6x + 9 = 0 has D = 0. What are its roots?
quiz.explain: D = 36 − 36 = 0, so both roots equal −b/2a = 6/2 = 3. Indeed x² − 6x + 9 = (x − 3)².
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal roots must have opposite signs

quiz.q: What is the discriminant of x² − 4x − 5 = 0?
quiz.explain: D = (−4)² − 4(1)(−5) = 16 + 20 = 36. Since D > 0 (and a perfect square), the roots 5 and −1 are distinct and rational.
quiz.mistake: Treats −4ac as −20 instead of +20

quiz.q: Why must a ≠ 0 in the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0?
options: Otherwise the equation becomes linear, not quadratic
quiz.explain: If a = 0, the x² term disappears and bx + c = 0 is linear.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that the x² term is what makes it quadratic

quiz.q: 4x² + 12x + 9 = 0 has equal roots. What is each root?
quiz.mistake: Uses b/2a without the minus sign

quiz.q: What are the roots of x² − 3x − 1 = 0?
quiz.mistake: Uses −b as −3 instead of +3

teach.ask: Gappu wants to solve x² + x + 2 = 0 with the formula straight away. What should he check first, and why?
teach.praise: Chirp! First find D — if it is negative there are no real roots, so no need for the formula!
teach.nudge: What does the sign of D tell me before I start solving?
